question: How many new-mover leads are in Lancaster County?
html:
New-Mover Leads in Lancaster County

The context has no Lancaster-only count. The ad plan gives new-mover volume only for the nine-county PA core: about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month. At the plan's assumed 1.0% mail lead rate, that is roughly 23 leads a month across the whole core (est.). Lancaster's share is not broken out (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What the data shows

MeasureFigureScope
Arm's-length residential sales~2,300 / monthPA core, nine counties
Arm's-length residential sales~1,150 / monthJersey Shore
Buyers of pre-1980 homes1 in 3PA core buyers
Assumed mail lead rate1.0% per piecePlan assumption
Implied mail leads~23 / month (est.)PA core
  • The 2,300 figure counts new-mover prospects: households that must pick an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider. These are not booked leads (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The 1.0% lead rate is deliberately set below the ANA prospect response of 4-5%. It is an assumption, not a measured result (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The Census permit snapshot for Sep 2026 covers new construction, not resales. It is not a proxy for movers (Census building permits).

Why Lancaster matters here

  • Lancaster is a confirmed tri-brand site on Running Pump Rd (Punctual Pros market profile).
  • 25.2% of Lancaster households heat with fuel oil or propane. That is relevant for Ben Franklin and One Hour offers (Punctual Pros market profile).
  • Competition is densest in Lancaster, Dauphin and nearby counties. Haller Enterprises alone has about 9,355 reviews and serves Lancaster (Punctual Pros market profile).
  • Splitting the 2,300 by household share would be a guess. The profile does not list Lancaster's household count or its deed volume. Do not use a pro-rata number until the county split is pulled.

Data that would answer it

  • Monthly arm's-length deed transfers from the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds, filtered to residential.
  • Mail-drop counts and responses by county from ServiceTitan tracking numbers and QR codes. The week-one test plan already sets these up per channel and creative.
  • The week-four read on booked jobs per 10k housing units, exposed versus holdout. This read would replace the 1.0% assumption with a measured rate.

Next actions

  1. Pull 12 months of Lancaster residential deed transfers. Add a county column to the new-mover list so every drop can be counted by county.
  2. Tag mail tracking numbers by county in ServiceTitan before the next drop.
  3. Report Lancaster mail response separately at the week-four read. Then restate leads as measured, not assumed.
  4. Check that Lancaster's 10% new-mover holdout is large enough to read on its own. If it is not, pool Lancaster with adjacent counties and note that the result is directional.
markdown:
# New-Mover Leads in Lancaster County

The context has no Lancaster-only count. The ad plan gives new-mover volume only for the nine-county PA core: about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month. At the plan's assumed 1.0% mail lead rate, that is roughly 23 leads a month across the whole core (est.). Lancaster's share is not broken out (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What the data shows

| Measure | Figure | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Arm's-length residential sales | ~2,300 / month | PA core, nine counties |
| Arm's-length residential sales | ~1,150 / month | Jersey Shore |
| Buyers of pre-1980 homes | 1 in 3 | PA core buyers |
| Assumed mail lead rate | 1.0% per piece | Plan assumption |
| Implied mail leads | ~23 / month (est.) | PA core |

- The 2,300 figure counts new-mover *prospects*: households that must pick an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider. These are not booked leads (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- The 1.0% lead rate is deliberately set below the ANA prospect response of 4-5%. It is an assumption, not a measured result (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- The Census permit snapshot for Sep 2026 covers new construction, not resales. It is not a proxy for movers (Census building permits).

## Why Lancaster matters here

- Lancaster is a confirmed tri-brand site on Running Pump Rd (Punctual Pros market profile).
- 25.2% of Lancaster households heat with fuel oil or propane. That is relevant for Ben Franklin and One Hour offers (Punctual Pros market profile).
- Competition is densest in Lancaster, Dauphin and nearby counties. Haller Enterprises alone has about 9,355 reviews and serves Lancaster (Punctual Pros market profile).
- Splitting the 2,300 by household share would be a guess. The profile does not list Lancaster's household count or its deed volume. Do not use a pro-rata number until the county split is pulled.

## Data that would answer it

- Monthly arm's-length deed transfers from the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds, filtered to residential.
- Mail-drop counts and responses by county from ServiceTitan tracking numbers and QR codes. The week-one test plan already sets these up per channel and creative.
- The week-four read on booked jobs per 10k housing units, exposed versus holdout. This read would replace the 1.0% assumption with a measured rate.

## Next actions

1. Pull 12 months of Lancaster residential deed transfers. Add a county column to the new-mover list so every drop can be counted by county.
2. Tag mail tracking numbers by county in ServiceTitan before the next drop.
3. Report Lancaster mail response separately at the week-four read. Then restate leads as measured, not assumed.
4. Check that Lancaster's 10% new-mover holdout is large enough to read on its own. If it is not, pool Lancaster with adjacent counties and note that the result is directional.
